cards.text: Picture it, friend: the LORD speaks to Joshua, Israel's leader, and tells him to have the Israelites designate the cities of refuge. And this isn't brand new, because God already gave these instructions once, through someone else. Me? I need to hear 'preheat the oven' THREE times before it sticks.

cards.question: The LORD tells Joshua He already gave the instructions for the cities of refuge through ___.

answers.text: Moses
Aaron
Samuel

cards.text: Here's the setup, friend. Somebody's gonna need to RUN with the avenger of blood on his heels, and God says these cities are where he runs TO.

cards.question: Who does God say can flee to a city of refuge?

answers.text: Someone who kills another by accident
Someone who steals from a neighbor
Someone who breaks a promise

cards.text: So he runs, and he makes it to the entrance of one city's gate. I'm a stamper who hops on a gold base, friend, so if anybody chased ME, I'd arrive sometime next Tuesday.

cards.question: Standing at the entrance of the city gate, the man states his case before the city's ___.

answers.text: elders
priests
Levites

cards.question: After the man states his case at the city gate, the elders make him camp outside the walls.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: But hold on. Hold on, hold on, HOLD ON. What if the avenger of blood comes chasing him all the way to that city?

cards.question: When the avenger of blood pursues the man to the city of refuge, the elders must not hand him over.

answers.text: True
False

cards.question: Why must the elders protect the man from the avenger of blood?

answers.text: He killed his neighbor with no prior malice
He already paid a fine to the family
He was born inside that city

cards.text: He's inside now. But this is NOT a quick stop, like ducking under an awning till the rain quits.

cards.question: How long does the man have to stay in the city of refuge?

answers.text: Until his trial and the high priest's death
Until the avenger of blood gives up
Until seven full years have passed

cards.question: Even after the high priest serving at that time dies, the man has to stay in the city of refuge for the rest of his life.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: So they set apart Kedesh in Galilee, Shechem and Hebron in the hill country, then Bezer, Ramoth in Gilead and Golan in Bashan beyond the Jordan, east of Jericho. SIX safe places, friend, and back in the junk drawer my only safe place was hiding under a takeout menu.
Then the passage spells out exactly who these cities are for. This is the fine print, friend, and unlike the warranty cards I shared that drawer with, somebody actually READS it.

cards.question: Who are the six cities of refuge appointed for?

answers.text: All the Israelites and the foreigners among them
Only the Israelites born in the land
Only the tribes that host the cities

cards.question: As the passage wraps up, what does it say the cities of refuge are for?

answers.text: So the manslayer isn't killed before his trial
So the tribes have safe places to trade
So the priests have more land to farm

findings.problem: The opening card has four sentences: 'Picture it, friend…', 'And this isn't brand new…', 'Me?' and 'I need to hear…'. The limit is three. Cut a sentence or merge 'Me?' into the joke line.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The card says the manslayer runs 'with the avenger of blood on his heels.' Verse 3 only says the cities are a refuge from the avenger of blood. Pursuit comes up only as a condition in verse 5 ('if the avenger of blood pursues him'), so stating it as certain stretches the text.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: Both wrong answers start with 'Only' and the right answer is the only inclusive one ('All the Israelites and the foreigners among them'). That pattern makes the right answer stand out. The answers should sound alike.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: Verse 9 restates the purpose already given in verse 3 (flee so as not to die by the avenger of blood). Card 4 already asked that, and card 12 already asked the 'before trial' part. Card 17 asks about the repeated statement again and adds nothing new to test. Ask about what verse 9 adds (it already does with card 16), or drop this card.

rule.text: When a line repeats, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears.

findings.problem: Verses 4–6 are the LORD's instructions about a hypothetical case ('When someone flees…', 'if the avenger of blood pursues him'). From card 5 on, the cards narrate the case as events happening ('So he runs, and he makes it…', 'He's inside now'). They never note that this is still God describing what should happen.
findings.question: When a passage gives a law as a hypothetical case, may Papa Dorin narrate it as a running story with a 'he' who acts? Or must the cards keep it framed as God's instructions (for example, 'God says when he gets there…')?
